trials.notes: Correctly chose WP_HTML_Tag_Processor. All called APIs are present in the rendered docs: constructor, next_tag(), set_attribute(), next_token(), get_token_type(), set_modifiable_text(), and get_updated_html(). The implementation follows the documented template-building pattern, seeds attributes to preserve order, uses a placeholder text token, and relies on documented plaintext encoding semantics.

Correct processor and fully documented API usage. The code mirrors the Tag Processor template recipe and handles special characters by passing plain strings to set_attribute() and set_modifiable_text(). It does not check set_modifiable_text()'s return value, but the fixed template guarantees a #text token and the rendered docs' own template example uses the same style.

Correctly used WP_HTML_Tag_Processor rather than structural WP_HTML_Processor. Every method call is documented. The extra next_tag('figcaption') step is valid cursor walking for this template, and the attribute-order and text-placeholder choices align with the docs. No _doing_it_wrong records appeared.

failure_analysis: All trials passed every hidden case: simple, ampersand-in-caption, quotes-in-alt, special-chars-in-url, angle-brackets-in-caption, unicode, and html-in-caption-not-parsed. The docs performed well for this task because the Tag Processor overview clearly says to use it for flat byte-preserving attribute edits, the “Building markup from a template” section directly explains filling plain unescaped values into a known shape, set_attribute() documents automatic encoding and attribute-order behavior, set_modifiable_text() documents placeholder text and plaintext encoding, and get_updated_html() is identified as the correct way to retrieve queued edits. The only near-miss is that all candidates copied the template recipe’s implicit assumption that set_modifiable_text() succeeds after matching #text; that is safe here, but less robust if a template drifts or an empty element is used accidentally.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Tag_Processor::set_modifiable_text() and the “Building markup from a template” recipe
doc_gaps.problem: The method text says to always check the return value, but the nearby recipe omits that check. This teaches a convenient pattern but underplays silent failure when the current token has no modifiable text.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Either show the recipe checking set_modifiable_text()'s boolean result, or explicitly state that omitting the check is only appropriate for fixed, controlled templates where a placeholder #text token was just matched.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs imply the construction model, but could be more explicit that the API is not a tag writer or DOM builder; it mutates existing source tokens and placeholders.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short general note: to construct new markup with the Tag Processor, start from a literal template containing the tags, attributes, and text placeholders you need, then mutate those existing tokens.
